content.title: Trail Etiquette
content.summary: Arvada's trail network spans over 150 miles and is designed for non-motorized recreation and commuting, with specific regulations prohibiting motorized vehicles, off-leash pets, and other activities. Class 1 and 2 e-bikes are permitted, provided they adhere to a 15 mph speed limit. Trail etiquette emphasizes safety and courtesy, including yielding to pedestrians and horses, keeping dogs leashed, and stepping off the trail when stopping.
content.body:
![people riding a bike waving](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=1809 "people riding a bike waving")

Arvada's 150-plus-mile trail network consists of [Primary](/558), [Local](/560) and [Regional](/866) Trails with both paved and soft surfaces. Trails are suitable for non-motorized recreational enjoyment as well as commuting.

## The following are not allowed in our parks, trails, open space and athletic complexes:

- **Motorized vehicles, including dirt bikes, golf carts and ATVs**
- Class 3 electric bicycles (Class 1 and 2 e-bikes are allowed)
- Off-leash pets
- Fires or camping
- Hunting or trapping
- Alcohol or smoking
- Open-carry firearms, air guns or other weapons
- Glass containers or littering
- Golfing

Class 1 and 2 e-bikes and electric scooters are allowed on trails, as long as they obey the speed limit of 15 mph.

Visit the [Arvada Police Department's page](/1364) to learn more about what types of bikes, vehicles and modes of transportation are allowed and not allowed on City streets and on trails and parks.

## Trail Etiquette Tips

Follow these tips to help make our trails safe and enjoyable for everyone!

![Trail Etiquette Tips Bike Speed Limit](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=1817 "Trail Etiquette Tips Bike Speed Limit")

![Trail Etiquette Tips: Keep dogs on a leash and pick up their waste](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=1815 "Trail Etiquette Tips: Keep dogs on a leash and pick up their waste")

![Trail Etiquette Tips: Bikes yield to pedestrians and horses. Pedestrians yield to horses. ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=2134 "Trail Etiquette Tips: Bikes yield to pedestrians and horses. Pedestrians yield to horses. ")

![Trail Etiquette Tips: Step off the trail when stopping to rest or chat](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=2133 "Trail Etiquette Tips: Step off the trail when stopping to rest or chat")

![Trail Etiquette Tips: Let others know when you're passing. ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=2135 "Trail Etiquette Tips: Let others know when you're passing. ")

![Trail Etiquette Tips Bonus Tip No Motor Vehicles](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=6055 "Trail Etiquette Tips Bonus Tip No Motor Vehicles")

### Top 5 Trail Etiquette Tips

1. The speed limit for all bikes, including e-bikes, is 15 miles per hour.

2. Keep dogs on a leash and clean up their waste.

3. Bikes yield to pedestrians and horses. Pedestrians yield to horses.

4. Step off the trail when stopping to rest or chat.

5. Let others know when you're passing.

Bonus Tip: No motor vehicles (this includes golf carts!)

It is against [City Code](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOOR_CH54MOVETR_ARTIIIMOVEPUPR) to drive an unlicensed motor vehicle, such as a golf cart, on any City street, trail or sidewalk.
